title: Justice Without Power (Taunt)
text: “Owowow! Grrrgh…”
“Weak, weeeak!”
Filo-tan unleashed the bratty-girl taunt-speak she’d picked up from Rafumi straight onto Smoked Meat, indeed.
“Hey now, Filo? Try not to rile them up too much.”
“Ehh?”
“Yes, yes, just like that. Isn’t it great? Filo-san, give them more.”
“Hold on, Itsuki?”
“You mustn’t let Filo-tan pick up such strange language!”
“Weak, so weeeak. Going on about jus-tice and all, but you’re so pathetic. Someone once said justice without power is powerless — powerless!”
“Her trash-talking’s leveled up when I wasn’t looking… Rafumi-chan’s definitely been coaching her behind the scenes… I hope it’s fine. It’d be a disaster if the other kids started copying her.”
“You wreeeetch―!”
With a snap, the instant Smoked Meat bared its hostility, its ear was pierced clean through.
“Eh, wha… wha, what?”

Since the paralysis had dulled its sense of pain, Smoked Meat wore an expression for a moment that said it had no idea what had just happened. Itsuki swiftly picked up the severed ear and tossed it down right in front of its face.
“―!? Gyaaaaaaah!?”
“How noisy! Screaming over something this minor is pathetic!”
With a thwack, Itsuki fired off something like a Silence Arrow straight into Smoked Meat.

“You shouldn’t make such a fuss over something that barely hurts. You’re only able to raise your voice like that because you don’t know how much pain, how many screams, the slaves of this country have endured. No — even if you knew, you probably wouldn’t understand.”
“Well then,” Itsuki said, a chilling smile spreading across his face as he gazed down at the Malds before turning to Father.

“Having it come to this actually leaves me feeling rather refreshed. To think this was their true nature all along… honestly, Naofumi-san, I can’t hold my head up around you. I’m truly sorry. All I can do is apologize over and over again, honestly!”
“I— Itsuki, I’m not bothered by it anymore, so… just don’t overdo it, alright? Besides, it’s Filo’s fault for provoking them.”
“Hmm?”
“That won’t do. I got carried away and became cruel toward you without limit, all while convinced I was in the right. Perhaps I should prostrate myself flat on the ground and apologize.”
“You’re being so self-deprecating it’s starting to sound sarcastic, Itsuki.”
“Haah…” Father let out a sigh deeper than I’d ever heard from him before.
“So in the end, what exactly were these lot scheming? I take it something’s been exposed?”

Since I couldn’t understand pig-speak, I asked Father to translate. Yuki-chan could have done it too, but her own interpretations tend to creep in, and it’d be a disaster if something got twisted. Better to have Father explain it, I decided.

“Well… how should I put it? Seems like these guys realized what happened — that Itsuki got tricked into becoming a riska and got sold off — and after that they just kept doing whatever they wanted while holding onto their power.”

Apparently they’d caught on around the time Ren showed up. Well, of course — the story about Ren turning into an inult happened on the very same day Itsuki went missing, the same day some similarly-sized demi-human had been passed off as Itsuki and sold for a single night’s worth of drinking money. Naturally, Smoked Meat and the others had tried using their connections to buy Itsuki back, but it was too late — the dealer who’d sold him off had apparently been careless, and his whereabouts had become impossible to track. So it seems these Malds came up with a plan: if they ever found Itsuki anywhere, they’d kill him without question to silence him, then pin all the blame on Father, the Shield Hero. “Itsuki-sama, the Bow Hero, was murdered by the Shield Hero!” — something along those lines. From Itsuki’s perspective, it was exactly the theory he’d imagined — that anything was permissible so long as it framed Father for a crime he never committed. And then that Itsuki, as a riska, had been briefly spotted at the circus. No mistake about it. But if Father or I were around, they might get stopped. So they’d waited for a moment when we were away and launched their raid — that was apparently the gist of it. Utterly foolish through and through, and it was precisely because of their petty, half-baked scheming that they’d ended up captured like this, indeed.
“I keep thinking, wouldn’t it have made more sense to strike during the show itself?”
“That’s probably a trick they picked up from me, wouldn’t you say? I used that method plenty of times myself — storming in at night to capture wrongdoers.”

“That might be part of it, but I’d guess they also didn’t want Itsuki slipping away in front of a lot of witnesses. No matter how loudly they shouted that he was a wanted demi-human, everyone around would still see them murdering one who wasn’t even resisting, without any due process. And if he did resist and showed hero-level power in front of ordinary people, that’d be even worse for them.”
“That’s a possibility too, I suppose. Either way, given how they’re groveling on the ground right now, the outcome was pretty much decided.”
“Truly foolish.”
“Yes, I never intended to forgive them. If they’d just bowed their heads without doing anything more, I might have shown a little mercy.”
“By the way, where’s Ren?”
“He’s off running from Luna-san, so he’s not here.”
Ah, so that’s why he’d been nowhere in sight this whole time.
“I wonder if Keel-kun’s with him? Should we get word to them? Might be faster to just ask Rafumi-chan.”
“Whatever the case…”
Itsuki said, trampling on the fallen Malds while his hair stood on end and he laughed wickedly.
“Itsuki, you’re laughing wickedly.”
“Oops, can’t hide my expression, can I.”
Itsuki laughed like a summer moth flying straight into the flame.

“What should we do about this… by the way, from what I’ve heard, the Bow Hero’s party’s reputation has gotten absolutely terrible. Guess whatever else you can say, it must’ve been Itsuki keeping things in check after all.”
Apparently one of them had been playing body double for Itsuki, wearing a mask and carrying a bow. The ruse had been exposed rather easily.
“Naofumi-san. Their treatment’s already decided, isn’t it? We sell them off to Siltvelt nobility. For torture purposes, of course.”
Smoked Meat and the rest, Itsuki’s former companions, all tried to resist together, but none of them seemed able to move an inch.

“Let’s have you relive the hell I went through, shall we? Ah, of course, do try your best to survive. Surely humans, being superior beings to demi-humans and beastmen, should find it easy to survive. You’re the higher existence, aren’t you? Do your best.”
“Now then!” Itsuki declared, ordering the monster merchant’s underlings and Father’s group to enslave the Malds, indeed.

“They used to be his companions, but any attachment or fondness he might’ve felt has clearly been blown to bits… it’s their own doing, really. Maybe if they’d looked at the situation a little more carefully, things could’ve gone differently — but we’ve taken damage too, so.”
Given that there were casualties on our side, Father had no intention of showing mercy either.
“Oink, oink-oink.”
Oh? Seemed like the paralysis on one of the pigs was a bit weaker, since it was talking.

“Ah, worried that people will get suspicious if you lot who came charging in never return? Too bad. We happen to have someone here who’ll handle that side of things in an entertaining way, so there’s no problem at all.”
“What is it? Did somebody call?”
And with that, Rafumi made her appearance.
“Hmm, I see.”
With a poof, Rafumi transformed into a copy of the Malds, indeed.
“Seems like the criminals we were looking for weren’t in this tent after all! Well then, excuse us! We’ve got justice to attend to, we’re busy people!”
She said, in a voice identical to Smoked Meat’s, and strode out of the tent.

“After that, all that’s left is to make sure some witnesses spot them near an inn or somewhere, and then vanish. That should be plenty… Understand now? Yes, that’s the face I wanted to see. Hahahaha.”
Itsuki said this with an expression that really shouldn’t be seen by anyone. Rabbit Guy and Riska, who’d appeared at some point without my noticing, watched that expression with furrowed brows.
“Bueeeeh…”

“I know they’re just villains wearing the skin of justice, so I suppose it can’t be helped… let’s just call it an inescapable karmic debt and be done with it. Otherwise… there’s nothing to be done about it. If they’d just apologized honestly, I could’ve made some case in their defense, at least a little.”

And so it was that Smoked Meat and the others, under Itsuki’s orders, were enslaved and sent off to Siltvelt to relive the very slave experience Itsuki himself had once endured. I ended up seeing a follow-up report on it later — apparently Smoked Meat screamed most beautifully, and the torture enthusiasts enjoyed it like it was some kind of musical instrument.
“Let’s have a drink tonight with the money we made off selling those guys! Come on, it’s my treat! Everyone, enjoy yourselves!”
“There’s no way we can enjoy this.”
“Those guys got to have their fun, so I won’t be satisfied unless I enjoy myself at full tension too! Come now, Rishia-san, you too, Rabbit — down it in one go.”
“This is the first time I’ve ever been to a celebration this joyless.”
“Bueeeeh……”
And so it went — Itsuki latching onto Rabbit Guy and the others with tremendous energy, which left quite the impression on me.
